channel.title: Jiǎoluò Shūwū · 角落書屋
channel.description: A reading nook for Chinese language and civilisation. Characters, vocabulary, grammar, history, philosophy, and the world they shaped.

item.title: 生旦净末丑 · Role Types in Peking Opera
item.description: Five role categories, each a complete performance tradition -- voice, movement, makeup, and costume as a total semiotic system.

item.title: 山水画 · landscape painting
item.description: Chinese landscape painting encodes a theory in its name: 山 (mountain, yang, permanent) and 水 (water, yin, changing) in dynamic tension. A space to inhabit in the imagination, not a view to frame.

item.title: 诗经 · Book of Songs
item.description: China oldest poetry anthology: three hundred poems that Confucius said no educated person could afford to ignore.

item.title: 书法风格 · The Five Scripts of Chinese Calligraphy
item.description: Five script styles chart two thousand years of Chinese writing, from the solemn bronze inscriptions of the Zhou to the explosive cursive of the Tang masters.

item.title: 水墨画 · Ink-Wash Painting
item.description: Where the brush meets philosophy: five tones of ink, the art of leaving space, and landscapes that are not about landscape at all.

item.title: 宋词 · Song Dynasty Lyric
item.description: The poem that sings: fixed tune patterns, named meters, and three masters who defined what the Chinese lyric could feel.

item.title: 唐诗 · Tang Poetry
item.description: Li Bai, Du Fu, and the golden age of regulated verse.

item.title: 篆刻 · Seal Carving
item.description: The art of the name: bronze to stone, dynasty to dynasty, two schools of carvers, and the small red square that authenticates everything.

item.title: 可 · can; may; worth; quite
item.description: A two-stroke mouth character whose ancient sense of affirming breath became the pivot of permission, capability, and worth in classical and modern Chinese.

item.title: 快 · fast, happy
item.description: One character carries two meanings that turn out to be the same thing: speed and joy both feel like the heart cutting loose.

item.title: 山 · mountain, hill, sacred peak
item.description: Three peaks rising from the earth: the oldest pictograph and the axis of Chinese sacred geography.

item.title: 也 · also; too; classical particle
item.description: A pictograph that lost its original image entirely and became one of the most load-bearing particles in classical Chinese: the gavel at the end of every verdict.

item.title: 雨 · rain
item.description: The oracle bone shows rain falling from the sky: one of the most transparent pictographs in the script, and the radical that organizes all Chinese weather.

item.title: 玉 · jade, precious
item.description: The material of kingship and moral cultivation: three jade discs on a cord, a glyph almost identical to king, the stone that Confucius said was virtue made visible.

item.title: 了 · the perfective particle
item.description: Perfective aspect vs. change-of-state: the single most-confused particle.

item.title: 着 · the continuous aspect marker
item.description: Three distinct jobs: holding a state, linking two actions, and commanding attention. All from a single particle that beginners collapse into one.

item.title: 理学 · Neo-Confucianism
item.description: Zhu Xi, the Great Ultimate 太极, and the Song-Ming synthesis.

item.title: 荀子 · Xunzi
item.description: Human nature as bad: ritual and education as correction.

item.title: 王阳明 · Wang Yangming and the School of Mind
item.description: Wang Yangming broke Neo-Confucianism open: instead of investigating external things to reach moral truth, he turned inward and declared that the moral mind already knows, and that knowing and acting are one indivisible movement.

item.title: 庄子 · Zhuangzi
item.description: The butterfly dream, Cook Ding, and Daoist freedom from convention.

item.title: 城隍 · The City God
item.description: Every Chinese city had a City God who served as its divine magistrate, managing the dead and the living with the same bureaucratic precision as any imperial official.

item.title: 历史 · history
item.description: The character for historian shows a hand holding a brush over a vessel: in ancient China, the scribe who held the brush held power.

item.title: 轮回 · samsara; the cycle of rebirth
item.description: The Buddhist karmic wheel that turns through six realms of existence: the foundational concept that motivates all Buddhist practice as a path toward liberation.

item.title: 缘分 · karmic connection
item.description: Buddhist-rooted fate that ties strangers, lovers, and old friends.

item.title: 八 · eight; the luckiest number and the eight trigrams
item.description: Eight is the most coveted number in modern China through its near-homophony with 发 fā (to prosper), and the classical foundation of the eight trigrams that structure the Yijing.

item.title: 黑 · black, darkness, and the illicit
item.description: Black on the surface, but the live sense is moral: the black market, the underworld, the hacker. The color that names everything that operates out of sight.

item.title: 很 · very; the empty intensifier
item.description: 很 is the word for very, but its strangest job is doing nothing: Chinese needs a degree adverb before a plain adjective, and 很 fills that slot so quietly that 我很好 means simply I am fine, not I am very well.

item.title: 红 · red, the color of luck and celebration
item.description: The cultural keystone color: weddings, New Year, the red envelope, and a century of revolutionary politics all run through this one character.

item.title: 九 · nine; the imperial number and the highest of the yang
item.description: Nine is the largest single digit and the highest yang number, reserved for the emperor and the heavens: nine dragons, nine gates, the Nine-Five supreme position, the ninth heaven.

item.title: 两 · two (of); a pair; the tael, the other word for two
item.description: 两 is the two used before measure words, the two of quantity and pairing, as opposed to 二 the two of counting and order, a distinction that is one of the first real puzzles a learner meets.
